[[File:Joachim Schwermer.jpg|thumb|Schwermer at [[Oberwolfach]], 2010]]
'''Joachim Schwermer''' (26 May 1950, [[Kulmbach]]<ref>brief biography in [http://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/ar/annualreportforf1981inst.pdf The Institute for Advanced Study, ''Annual Report for the Fiscal Year July 1, 1980-June 30, 1981''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111219141051/http://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/ar/annualreportforf1981inst.pdf |date=December 19, 2011 }} (PDF; 4,6&nbsp;MB), p. 41</ref>) is a German mathematician, specializing in [[number theory]].

==Education==
Schwermer received his ''[[Abitur]]'' in 1969 at [[Aloisiuskolleg]] in [[Bad Godesberg]] and then studied mathematics at the [[University of Bonn]].{{cn|date=May 2024}} After graduating in 1974 with his ''[[Diplom]]'', he received in 1977 his [[Promotion (Germany)|''Promotion'']] (Ph.D.) under [[Günter Harder]] with thesis ''Eisensteinreihen und die Kohomologie von Kongruenzuntergruppen von <math>SL_n(\mathbb{Z})</math>''.<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=23445|name=Joachim Schwermer}}</ref> In 1982 he received his ''[[Habilitation]]'' from the [[University of Bonn]].

==Career==
From 1986 he was a professor at the [[Catholic University of Eichstätt-Ingolstadt]], then at the [[University of Düsseldorf]],<ref>See the author addresses in ''[https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02785578 On the concept of level for subgroups of SL<sub>2</sub> over arithmetic rings]'' (May 1998)</ref> and finally in the 2000s at the [[University of Vienna]]. During the academic year 1980–1981 Schwermer was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. He is the scientific director at the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics]].

==Research==
Schwermer's research deals with algebraic groups in number theory, [[arithmetic geometry]], [[Lie group]]s, and [[L-function]]s. He has written essays on the history of mathematics, for example, about [[Helmut Hasse]], [[Hermann Minkowski]], and [[Emil Artin]].

==Awards and honors==
In 1987 he was awarded the [[Gay-Lussac-Humboldt-Prize]].

==Selected publications==
* with [[Della Dumbaugh]], ''[[Emil Artin]] and Beyond – Class Field Theory and L-Functions'', Heritage of European Mathematics, [[European Mathematical Society]], 2015, {{ISBN|978-3037191460}}
* with [[Jens Carsten Jantzen]]: ''Algebra'', Springer, 2006, {{ISBN|3540213805}}, {{doi|10.1007/3-540-29287-X}}
* ''Kohomologie arithmetisch definierter Gruppen und Eisensteinreihen'', Springer, Lectures Notes in Mathematics Bd.988, 1983, {{ISBN|9783540122920}}, {{doi|10.1007/BFb0070268}}
* as editor with [[Jean-Pierre Labesse]]: ''Cohomology of arithmetic groups and automorphic forms'', Springer, 1990, Lecture Notes in Mathematics (Konferenz Luminy/Marseille 1989), {{doi|10.1007/BFb0085723}}
* as editor with [[Catherine Goldstein]] and [[Norbert Schappacher]]: ''The Shaping of Arithmetic after C. F. Gauss's [[Disquisitiones Arithmeticae]]'', Springer 2007. {{ISBN|978-3-540-20441-1}} (containing Schwermer's essay ''Reduction theory of quadratic forms: towards räumliche Anschauung in Minkowski's Early Work '', {{doi|10.1007/978-3-540-34720-0_18}}, and his essay, with [[Della Dumbaugh|Della Fenster]], [https://books.google.com/books?id=IUFTcOsMTysC&pg=PA145 ''Composition of Quadratic Forms: An Algebraic Perspective''], {{doi|10.1007/978-3-540-34720-0_5}})
*''Minkowski, Hensel, and Hasse: On The Beginnings of the Local-Global Principle'', in [[Jeremy Gray (mathematician)|Jeremy Gray]], [[Karen Parshall]]: ''Episodes in the history of modern algebra (1800-1950)'', American Mathematical Society 2007
*''Über Reziprozitätsgesetze in der Zahlentheorie'', in [[Horst Knörrer]] (ed.): ''Arithmetik und Geometrie'', Mathematische Miniaturen, vol. 3, Birkhäuser Verlag 1986, {{ISBN|3-7643-1759-0}}, {{doi|10.1007/978-3-0348-5226-5_2}}
